title: Line-module preparation on an arbitrary scheme test of a locally polarized space
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:F\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $M$ a line module on $F$. Let $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective etale family from schemes, and suppose $F_i=F\times_YY_i$ is a scheme for every $i$. Write $M_i$ for the ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] obtained by restricting $M$ along $F_i\to F$ and then to Zariski opens [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. Suppose $M_i|_{F_i\times_{Y_i}V}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $V\subseteq Y_i$.
For any scheme $T$ over $S$ and any map $h_T\to Y$, put $X=F\times_YT$, $T_i=Y_i\times_YT$, and $X_i=X\times_TT_i\simeq F_i\times_{Y_i}T_i$. Then $X$ is an algebraic space, all $T_i,X_i$ are schemes, and $\{T_i\to T\}$ and $\{X_i\to X\}$ are jointly surjective etale families. Let $N_i$ be the ordinary tensor pullback of $M_i$ to $X_i$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. The $N_i$ are invertible and ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $T_i$. On $X_i\times_XX_j$, their transition isomorphisms obtained by pulling back the restriction identifications of $M$ on $F_i\times_FF_j$ satisfy the diagonal identity and the triple-overlap cocycle. There is a line module $N$ on $X$, with identifications $N|_{X_i}\simeq N_i$ inducing exactly these transitions; it is unique up to the unique isomorphism preserving the identifications. The projection $f_T:X\to T$ is quasi-compact and separated, in the terminology of [def-sfb-space-quasi-compact-presheaf-map] and [def-sfb-presheaf-map-separated-diagonal]. If $T\to Y$ is etale, the same local identifications induce a canonical isomorphism $N\simeq M|_X$ of line modules on $X$.

proof.text: Obtain the geometric charts on the arbitrary scheme test, choosing the actual scheme pullbacks as source schemes.

Apply normalized line descent to the original M, these charts, and their commuting triangles. This supplies original invertibility, every transition and cocycle, the descended line module, uniqueness, and the etale comparison.

Use clause (1) of invertible_pullback_tensor to make each literal pullback invertible. Apply scheme relative-ampleness base change to each actual scheme pullback; no transport across an arbitrary chosen chart is needed.

For each affine open of T_i, absolute ampleness supplies CompactSpace of its inverse image. The Mathlib affine-open criterion gives QuasiCompact of the local scheme map. The final separatedness clause of the canonical-Proj criterion gives IsSeparated.

Apply the scheme-chart recognition bridge to obtain both presheaf geometric properties. Build the complete preparation structure from the chart data, normalized line data, and these proved local module properties. The etale comparison is exactly the one carried by normalized line descent.

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] first to $F\to Y\leftarrow T$, then to the covering $(Y_i\to Y)_i$ after base change to $T$ and to $X=F\times_YT$. It gives the algebraic space $X$, schemes $T_i=Y_i\times_YT$, and the jointly surjective etale family $(T_i\to T)_i$. The other base change gives the covering $(X_i\to X)_i$. Associativity of fibre products identifies $X_i$ with $F_i\times_{Y_i}T_i$: both have the same tuples of compatible maps to $F,Y_i,T$. Since $F_i,Y_i,T_i$ are schemes, [def-pc-fibre-product] makes each $X_i$ a scheme. Representability of the diagonals also makes all double and triple overlaps of these scheme charts schemes.

source.place: Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces); spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F (lemma-etale), (3); the fibre-product tuple identifications are universal-property calculations.

old_proof.text: Write $a_i:X_i\to F_i$ and put $N_i=a_i^*M_i$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] makes $N_i$ invertible. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change] to $F_i\to Y_i$, the arbitrary scheme map $T_i\to Y_i$, and $M_i$. Its hypothesis is exactly the assumed ampleness over all affine opens of $Y_i$, so it proves ampleness of $N_i$ on the inverse image of every affine open of $T_i$. No etaleness or flatness of $T\to Y$ is needed.

On $R_{ij}=F_i\times_FF_j$ write $r_i,r_j$ for the projections. By [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison], the ordinary modules $r_i^*M_i,r_j^*M_j$ correspond to the restrictions of $M$ to the same localized site $(R_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}$. Restriction of a sheaf composes by composition of its indexing maps [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The identity between these two restrictions therefore gives a specified isomorphism $\alpha_{ij}:r_j^*M_j\simeq r_i^*M_i$. The comparison equivalence is fully faithful and compatible with composition of etale maps. Consequently its ordinary isomorphisms satisfy the diagonal identity and $\alpha_{ij}\alpha_{jk}=\alpha_{ik}$ on triple overlaps: both composites correspond to the identity of the same restriction of $M$. The comparisons of [lem-trf-etale-line-sections-normalized-comparisons] are the unit-normalized tensor comparisons, including their identity and composition laws. On opens, [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] identifies the tensor pullback with ordinary restriction. Thus restriction to opens here is precisely [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction].

Put $D_{ij}=X_i\times_XX_j$, with projections $p_i,p_j$. Its projections to $F_i,F_j$ induce $b_{ij}:D_{ij}\to R_{ij}$. Pull back $\alpha_{ij}$ by $b_{ij}$ and use composition of tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] to obtain $\beta_{ij}:p_j^*N_j\simeq p_i^*N_i$. These are exactly the transitions in the statement. The composition identifications are the tensor associativity maps: locally they send $c\otimes(d\otimes m)$ to $c\,a^\sharp(d)\otimes m$. For three pullbacks, either bracketing sends $c\otimes(d\otimes(e\otimes m))$ to $c\,a^\sharp(d)\,(a^\sharp b^\sharp)(e)\otimes m$. Thus there is no change of the cocycle under the composition identifications. Functoriality of pullback sends the identity and the equality $\alpha_{ij}\alpha_{jk}=\alpha_{ik}$ to the diagonal identity and $\beta_{ij}\beta_{jk}=\beta_{ik}$, respectively.

source.place: Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules), with the elementary associativity formula for the tensor pullback of Tag 0095.

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent] to the algebraic space $X$, the scheme covering $(X_i\to X)_i$, the ordinary invertible modules $N_i$, and the transitions $\beta_{ij}$ just verified. It gives a line module $N$ and identifications with the $N_i$ inducing exactly those transitions. For two such choices the induced local comparison isomorphisms agree on every double overlap. The Hom bijection in the same cited statement gives a unique global comparison. Apply it again to their inverses: both composites restrict to identities and hence are identities by injectivity of that Hom map. This is uniqueness up to the unique isomorphism preserving the identifications.

old_proof.text: Let $v_i:X_i\to T_i$ be the projection. For each affine open $V\subseteq T_i$, Step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] imply that $v_i^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] this says that $v_i$ is quasi-compact as a scheme morphism. Apply condition (1) of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] to $v_i,N_i$. It requires precisely this quasi-compactness, invertibility, and ampleness over every affine open. Its final assertion gives that $v_i$ is separated. We use only that final assertion, without constructing a Proj map or using the conclusion of the parent ampleness-descent item.

source.place: Tags 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample) and 01VI (lemma-relatively-ample-separated); spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3C, quasi-compact/separated preparation paragraph.

old_proof.text: These scheme properties also satisfy the space terminology of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Indeed, for an affine scheme $Z\to T_i$, [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] gives a quasi-compact morphism $X_i\times_{T_i}Z\to Z$. Its source is quasi-compact by evaluating the definition at the affine open $Z$ itself; its identity is a surjective etale atlas. For separatedness, [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes the scheme diagonal of $v_i$ a closed immersion. Every scheme test of that diagonal remains a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Now apply the reverse implication of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to $X\to T$ and the jointly surjective etale scheme family $(T_i\to T)_i$. All its local base changes are the $v_i$, so $f_T$ is quasi-compact and separated in exactly the stipulated sense.

old_proof.text: Finally suppose $T\to Y$ is etale. Then $\{T\to Y\}\cup\{g_i\}_{i}$ is a jointly surjective etale family, so [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], applied to it and $F\to Y$, makes its member $X=F\times_YT\to F$ etale, and $M|_X$ is defined by restriction. Since $X_i\simeq F_i\times_FX$, the map $a_i:X_i\to F_i$ is the scheme test of the etale map $X\to F$ at $F_i\to F$, hence etale by the definition of etale maps in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The etale pullback compatibility of [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] identifies $(M|_X)|_{X_i}$ with the line module associated to $a_i^*M_i=N_i$. On overlaps these identifications give $\beta_{ij}$ by their construction as restrictions of the same $M$, followed by tensor composition. The Hom bijection of [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent] therefore glues these local identifications to a unique $N\simeq M|_X$; gluing the inverse local maps proves it is an isomorphism. Its prescribed local character makes it canonical.
